title: No Hands: The Wild Ride of the Schwinn Bicycle Company
content:
Unfeatured Films, an independent studio focused on telling culturally resonant, character-driven stories, has released the first trailer for its upcoming feature documentary – No Hands: The Wild Ride of the Schwinn Bicycle Company…

No Hands is a nostalgic, mystery-driven sprint through a century of Americana, tracing the rise and fall of the iconic Schwinn Bicycle Company while opening into a larger story about childhood, cycling and American culture. Narrated by Lance Armstrong and directed by Unfeatured Films Founder Daniel Clarke, the film is coming for the first time to audiences in Southern California and Chicago.

After selling out every festival screening to date, from Boulder International Film Festival and Woods Hole Film Festival to Mill Valley Film Festival, and drawing strong emotional audience reactions, No Hands continues its fall festival run with upcoming screenings including:

  • Newport Beach Film Festival (Southern California premiere)
    • Sunday, October 18 at 4:30 p.m. at the Lido Theater
    • Tuesday, October 20 at 2:30 p.m. at Big Newport, Screen 4
  • Chicago International Film Festival (Midwest premiere)
    • Saturday, October 24 at 6:00 p.m. at the AMC Newcity
    • Sunday, October 25 at 3:00 p.m. at the Chicago History Museum.

More than a century after Schwinn’s founding – and more than three decades after its 1992 bankruptcy – the No Hands filmmakers reveal the dramatic, largely untold story of a legendary American brand that once rivaled Coca-Cola and McDonald’s in popularity. They trace the company’s rise, cultural impact and mysterious fall while examining how bicycles changed the way people moved through the world.

The documentary feature spans Schwinn’s storied history, from the iconic Sting-Ray to its influence on BMX and mountain biking.

Fans, collectors, and cycling pioneers – including Trek Bicycle President John Burke, mountain biking pioneers Gary Fisher, Joe Breeze and Charlie Kelly, and Richard Schwinn, great-grandson of co-founder Ignaz Schwinn – recount how the brand changed cycling forever while navigating the pressures of American manufacturing, family drama, fads and business forces…
